stage_receipts.reason: Three numbered NL segments were analyzed. NL1 is purely descriptive (names the modeled device and its role) and is marked context. NL2 establishes the initial state, an initial-entry transition into the braking state on brake-signal receipt, an alternative endpoint to an operational state upon signal-transmission failure, and a return endpoint from the braking state back to the initial state upon signal feedback; these are captured as one initial_entry contract plus a transition group with two alternatives (braking-state entry conditioned on brake signal is folded into the initial-entry semantics per discourse, while the failure alternative and the feedback-return are separate endpoint contracts) since the source discourse treats the initial state as the shared source for the signal-received/failure branch, and the braking state as source for the feedback-return branch. NL3 continues the narrative from the braking state onward to a new brake-caliper-clamping state, extracted as a separate endpoint contract. No cardinality, containment beyond the discourse-implied owner, guard-disjointness un-supported by explicit distinguishability language, or state_action obligations are explicitly established by this terse NL, so none were manufactured. Termination is not explicitly declared for any named state, so no termination contract was created; braking, operational, and brake-caliper-clamping states are treated as operating_state, and initial state as initial_state.
